newsitem.title: FRANCE: Charity urges safe passage for Zaire aid workers.
newsitem.headline: Charity urges safe passage for Zaire aid workers.

text.p: A medical charity urged warring parties in eastern Zaire on Friday to urgently allow some 100 international aid workers to evacuate the town of Goma and regain access to refugee camps.

Medecins sans Frontieres (Doctors without Borders) said some 100 aid workers, including six of its staff, were stranded by the fighting in the Goma compound of the United Nations High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) for the second successive day.
It said the road to Gisenyi in Rwanda, the only option for evacuation, was no longer safe as heavy fighting continued in and around Goma, and Gisenyi had come under fire.
"Medecins sans Frontieres (MsF) most urgently calls upon the warring parties to guarantee safe passage for aid workers in the area as well as for populations fleeing the violence of war," it said.
"MsF also asks for safe access for humanitarian organisations to the victims of the conflict to be restored as soon as possible," it said.
Diplomats said Rwandan troops in uniform entered Goma on Friday by lake and land to back Tutsi rebels who have already captured the Zairean town of Bukavu to the south.
Rwanda denied there were any of its troops in the town.

Zairean and Rwandan troops traded fire across the border at Gisenyi, at the north end of Lake Kivu just across the border from Goma, North Kivu's capital and previously the main base for Zaire's army and allied Rwandan Hutu forces.
Zaire's ragged army is facing a humiliating defeat against the well-armed rebels in the two eastern provinces of North and South Kivu facing Rwanda and Burundi.

All sides ignored international calls for a ceasefire. The United Nations, fearing a humanitarian disaster, agonised over whether it should pull out its staff and effectively abort its mission to feed 1.1 million Rwandan refugees inside Zaire.
